t.6.13.1: When Rāghava granted him safety, Rāvaṇa's younger brother bowed low and, overjoyed, descended from the sky to the earth together with his devoted followers.
t.6.13.3: Then Vibhīṣaṇa spoke there to Rāma words that were righteous and fitting, and that at once brought great delight.
t.6.13.4: I am the younger brother of Rāvaṇa, and I have been humiliated by him. I have come for refuge to you, who are the refuge of all beings.
t.6.13.6: In the slaying of the Rākṣasas and in the assault upon Laṅkā I shall render aid to the utmost of my strength, and I shall enter into their army.
t.6.13.5: Laṅkā has been abandoned by me, along with my friends and my riches. My kingdom, my life and my happiness now rest in you.
t.6.13.7: Rāma, pleased, embraced Vibhīṣaṇa as he spoke thus, and said to Lakṣmaṇa, "Bring water from the ocean."
t.6.13.8: And with that, O bestower of honor, quickly consecrate this greatly wise Vibhīṣaṇa as king of the rākṣasas, for I am pleased.
t.6.13.9: Thus addressed, Saumitri, at Rāma's command, consecrated Vibhīṣaṇa as king in the midst of the foremost of the vānaras.
t.6.13.2: But Vibhīṣaṇa, of righteous soul, seeking refuge, fell at the feet of Rāma together with his four rākṣasas.
t.6.13.10: Seeing that graciousness of Rāma, the monkeys at once raised loud shouts and cried, "Well done! Well done!"
t.6.13.11: And Hanumān and Sugrīva said to Vibhīṣaṇa: "How shall we cross the ocean, the unshakable abode of Varuṇa?"
t.6.13.12: Let us approach the lord of rivers and streams by such means that all of us, together with our armies, may swiftly cross the abode of Varuṇa.
t.6.13.13: Thus addressed, Vibhīṣaṇa, knower of dharma, replied: "King Rāghava ought to go to the Ocean for refuge."
t.6.13.14: This immeasurable great ocean was caused to be dug by Sagara; the great ocean ought to accomplish the task of Rāma, his kinsman.
t.6.13.15: When the wise rākṣasa Vibhīṣaṇa had spoken thus, his words pleased even Rāghava, whose very nature was steeped in righteousness.
t.6.13.16: He of great splendour, skilled in action, smiling first, spoke to Lakṣmaṇa and to Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, for the sake of showing honour.
t.6.13.17: This counsel of Vibhīṣaṇa pleases me, O Lakṣmaṇa. Tell me, you together with Sugrīva, whether it pleases you as well.
t.6.13.19: Thus addressed, those two heroes, Sugrīva and Lakṣmaṇa, both spoke these words, endowed with fitting courtesy.
t.6.13.18: Sugrīva is ever wise, and you are skilled in counsel. Having deliberated together, let the two of you declare whatever noble course seems best.
t.6.13.20: Why, O tiger among men, O Rāghava, should what Vibhīṣaṇa has said not please us, since it brings well-being at this time?
t.6.13.21: Without building a bridge across this terrible ocean, the abode of Varuṇa, Laṅkā cannot be reached even by the gods and asuras together with Indra.
t.6.13.23: Thus addressed, Rāma then lay down upon the kuśa-strewn shore of the lord of rivers and streams, like a sacrificial fire settled upon its altar.
t.6.13.22: Let the words of the heroic Vibhīṣaṇa be carried out as they were meant. Enough of causing delay; let this ocean be called upon.
